## 1. Notation Reference Table

| Symbol | Definition |
|--------|------------|
| $i = 1, \dots, m$ | Subject index ($m$ total subjects) |
| $j = 1, \dots, n_i$ | Visit index for subject $i$ ($n_i$ observations) |
| $Y_{ij}$ | Outcome for subject $i$ at visit $j$ |
| $\mathbf{X}_{ij}$ | Covariate vector for subject $i$ at visit $j$ |
| $\mu_{ij} = \mathbb{E}(Y_{ij} \mid \mathbf{X}_{ij})$ | Conditional mean |
| $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ | $n_i \times n_i$ covariance matrix for subject $i$ |
| $\mathbf{Y}_i = (Y_{i1}, \dots, Y_{in_i})^\top$ | Response vector for subject $i$ |
| $\mathbf{X}_i$ | $n_i \times p$ design matrix for subject $i$ |

**Covariate Types:**

| Type | Definition | Example |
|------|------------|---------|
| Time-constant | $X_{ij} = X_i$ for all $j$ | Sex, baseline age, treatment arm |
| Time-varying | $X_{ij}$ changes with $j$ | Current BP, visit time, cumulative dose |

---

## 2. Why Correlation Matters

**Paired vs Unpaired Variance for Mean Difference:**

| Design | $\mathrm{Var}(\bar{D})$ | Efficiency Gain |
|--------|-------------------------|-----------------|
| Unpaired (independent) | $\dfrac{2\sigma^2}{n}$ | — |
| Paired (same subjects) | $\dfrac{2\sigma^2(1-\rho)}{n}$ | Factor of $(1-\rho)$ |

**Key Rule:** Same subject measured at both times $\Rightarrow$ use **paired** analysis.

**Reliability & Attenuation:**

- Reliability: $\rho_{XX} = \dfrac{\sigma^2_{\text{true}}}{\sigma^2_{\text{true}} + \sigma^2_{\text{error}}}$
- Attenuation: $\hat{\beta}_{\text{obs}} = \rho_{XX} \cdot \beta_{\text{true}}$

---

## 3. First Look Workflow

| Step | Task | Purpose |
|:----:|------|---------|
| 1 | Distribution of $n_i$ (visits per subject) | Detect imbalance, dropout |
| 2 | Spaghetti plot (10 random IDs) | Visualize individual trajectories |
| 3 | Mean $\pm$ SE by visit/group | Population trend, group differences |
| 4 | Missingness pattern visualization | Identify MCAR/MAR/MNAR concerns |
| 5 | Correlation heatmap by visit | Inform covariance structure choice |

---

## 4. Three Modeling Approaches

| Approach | Time Treatment | Chapter | When to Use |
|----------|----------------|:-------:|-------------|
| **Response Profiles** | Time as factor | Ch. 5 | Few discrete time points; no trend assumption |
| **Parametric Trends** | Linear/quad/spline | Ch. 6 | Continuous time; smooth trajectory assumed |
| **Covariance Patterns** | CS/AR(1)/UN | Ch. 7 | Focus on variance structure; efficiency gains |

---

## 5. Common Data Structures

| Format | Structure | Best For |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| **Wide** | One row per subject, columns = visits | Time-constant covariates, multivariate analysis |
| **Long** | One row per observation | Mixed models, GEE, most R/SAS procedures |

**Key R Functions:**

```r
# Wide to Long
long_df <- pivot_longer(wide_df,
                        cols = starts_with("Y"),
                        names_to = "visit",
                        values_to = "outcome")

# Long to Wide
wide_df <- pivot_wider(long_df,
                       names_from = visit,
                       values_from = outcome)
```
